question: The output of a two-input AND gate is logic 1:

options.text: Only when both inputs are at logic 1
When either input, or both, is at logic 1
Only when the two inputs are different
Only when both inputs are at logic 0

explanation: AND requires every condition to be true. Any input at 0 makes the output 0.

question: The output of a two-input OR gate is logic 0:

options.text: Only when both inputs are at logic 0
Only when both inputs are at logic 1
Only when the two inputs are different
When either input is at logic 0

explanation: OR gives a 1 if any input is 1, so the only way to get a 0 out is for every input to be 0.

question: A NOT gate (inverter):

options.text: Gives logic 0 only when both of its two inputs are at 0
Gives an output that is always the opposite of its single input
Gives logic 1 only when both of its two inputs are at 1
Gives an output that is always the same as its input, delayed by one clock pulse

explanation: The inverter has one input and one output: 1 becomes 0 and 0 becomes 1. In circuit symbols, inversion is shown by a small circle (bubble) on the output or input.

question: A two-input NAND gate has inputs A = 1 and B = 0. Its output is:

options.text: The same as input B
Undefined

explanation: NAND is AND followed by NOT. A AND B = 0, so NAND gives 1. A NAND gate gives 0 only when all its inputs are 1.

question: A two-input NOR gate has inputs A = 1 and B = 0. Its output is:

options.text: The same as input A
Undefined

explanation: NOR is OR followed by NOT. A OR B = 1, so NOR gives 0. A NOR gate gives 1 only when all its inputs are 0.

question: The output of a NAND gate is logic 0:

options.text: When any one of its inputs is at logic 1
Only when all of its inputs are at logic 0
Only when all of its inputs are at logic 1
Only when its inputs are different

explanation: NAND inverts AND: AND gives 1 only with all inputs at 1, so NAND gives 0 only in that case and 1 in every other.

question: The output of a NOR gate is logic 1:

options.text: Only when its inputs are different
Only when all of its inputs are at logic 0
Only when all of its inputs are at logic 1
When any one of its inputs is at logic 1

explanation: NOR inverts OR: OR gives 0 only with all inputs at 0, so NOR gives 1 only in that case.

question: The output of a two-input exclusive-OR (XOR) gate is logic 1 when:

options.text: Either input, or both, is at logic 1
The two inputs are the same
Both inputs are at logic 1
The two inputs are different

explanation: XOR excludes the case where both are 1: it gives 1 for (1,0) and (0,1) only. That makes it a 'difference detector', used for example in comparing two channels.

question: A two-input XOR gate has both inputs at logic 1. Its output is:

options.text: 1 for one clock pulse, then 0
Undefined

explanation: With both inputs the same, an XOR gate gives 0. An ordinary OR gate would give 1 here — the one case where the two differ.

question: An exclusive-NOR (XNOR) gate gives logic 1 when:

options.text: Only both inputs are at 0
Only both inputs are at 1
Both inputs are the same
The two inputs are different

explanation: XNOR is the inverse of XOR, so it signals agreement (coincidence) between its inputs.

question: The output of an AND gate is fed into a NOT gate. The combination behaves as:

options.text: A NOR gate
An OR gate
An XOR gate
A NAND gate

explanation: Inverting the output of an AND gives NOT-AND — the NAND function. Likewise an OR followed by a NOT is a NOR.

question: NAND and NOR gates are called 'universal' gates because:

options.text: They give the same output as every other gate for every input
Any logic function can be built from one type alone
They can work with any supply voltage
They accept both analogue and digital inputs

explanation: With enough NAND gates (or enough NOR gates) you can make NOT, AND, OR and every other function. That is why integrated circuits are often built from one gate type.

question: A logic gate has three inputs. How many rows are needed in its truth table to cover every possible input combination?
explanation: Each input can be 0 or 1, so n inputs give 2ⁿ combinations: 2³ = 8.

question: A three-input AND gate has inputs of 1, 1 and 0. Its output is:

options.text: The majority of its inputs, which is 1
Undefined

explanation: An AND gate needs every input at 1. One input at 0 is enough to make the output 0, however many inputs there are.

question: A landing gear warning must sound if the gear is not down and locked and the thrust levers are retarded to idle. The basic logic function needed is:

options.text: NOR
AND
OR
XOR

explanation: Both conditions must be true together for the warning: 'gear not locked down' AND 'thrust at idle'. An OR would sound the warning whenever either condition alone existed, for example during the whole climb.

question: A warning light must come on if any one of three fuel pumps loses pressure. The basic logic function needed is:

options.text: AND
NAND
XNOR
OR

explanation: Any one input alone must trigger the output — the definition of OR. An AND would only warn when all three pumps had failed.

question: Some engine fire detection systems use two detection loops and give a fire warning only if both loops detect a fire. This 'AND' logic is used to:

options.text: Allow the fire to be extinguished automatically
Detect a fire more quickly than a single loop could
Ensure the warning sounds if either loop detects a fire
Reduce false fire warnings caused by a fault in a single loop

explanation: Requiring agreement between two independent loops means that one faulty loop cannot trigger a spurious warning. If a loop is known to be faulty, the system can usually be reconfigured to rely on the remaining one alone.

question: The binary number 1011 is equal to which decimal number?
explanation: Reading from the right, the place values are 1, 2, 4 and 8: (1 × 8) + (0 × 4) + (1 × 2) + (1 × 1) = 11.

question: A bistable (flip-flop) circuit is used in digital systems because it:

options.text: Holds its output after the setting input has gone, storing one bit
Returns to its original state automatically after a fixed time
Has no stable state and switches continuously at a set frequency
Changes an analogue input into a varying voltage output

explanation: A flip-flop has two stable states and stays in whichever it was last set to until told otherwise. It is the basic memory element of counters, registers and latched warnings.

question: According to De Morgan's theorem, NOT (A AND B) is equivalent to:

options.text: (NOT A) OR (NOT B)
(NOT A) AND (NOT B)
A OR B
NOT (A OR B)

explanation: Inverting an AND turns it into an OR of the inverted inputs. That is why a NAND gate is equivalent to an OR gate with inverted inputs, and NOT (A OR B) = (NOT A) AND (NOT B).
